Will of God

precepts.text: Thy will be done in earth. And the Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. The laws of God are within our hearts. So we want what God wants. That is why he says be ye perfect. He is telling us to be perfect, even as our Father is perfect. So the objective is for us to become one with him. Our objective is to become one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That is the hierarchy that the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs. We are his ambassadors on this earth. And that is why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of him. We are the prince of his power. That is us. That is not anybody else. That is us.
precepts.point: Thy kingdom come. So Christ said pray to the Lord for his kingdom to be done on earth. We are joint heirs with him. So what are we actually praying for? We are praying for our kingdom as well.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
“Thy will be done in earth.” The Lord's will will be done in earth, because this is the will that we want. David said it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The laws of God are within our hearts, so we want what God wants. That's why he says be ye perfect, even as our Father is perfect. The objective is to become one with him: one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That's the hierarchy the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs, his ambassadors on this earth, and that's why he gave us the name Israel. We are the prince of his power. That's us, not anybody else.

If the will of God is going to be done in this earth, and there is a will here already, then this will has got to be destroyed. Two kings cannot sit on the same throne. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” Notice: is given. Esau took the planet and ruled it in evil, yes, but God gave him the power to do so, for a time, and when that time is up it's over.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” Esau struts with his chest out, bombing countries and stealing their resources, their minds, their women, and everybody wants to look like him. And the Most High says, I'm the one who put him up there, so that I can destroy him and everybody will know I'm the true power. The Lord endures with longsuffering because he will not break his word: he gave this man a time to rule, until the times of the nations be fulfilled. The whole nation of Edom is the vessels of wrath, a channel through which God shows how angry and how powerful he is, fitted to destruction, created for that purpose, just as he set up Pharaoh.

These are diabolical, demonic people; look at James Byrd dragged through the streets of Jasper, Texas. That's not teaching hatred; it's the facts. There's no such thing as a nice snake. Stick by these commandments. Come out from among them, be separate, gather yourselves together, organize and prepare for your kingdom while he brings this kingdom down. That is the maturing we have to do.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. The will of God, the laws of God: to process, to understand, to see clearly, bouncing things off of the scriptures. You no longer conform to this world; you do not move like everybody else anymore.
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
What is the will of the Lord? David answers: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God, and they are within the heart.

That is what a renewed mind does with them: it moves by them, processes, understands, knows, sees clearly. You have understanding now, and you are bouncing things off of the scriptures.

So you no longer conform to this world. You do not move like everybody else anymore. You are using your mind for what it is for: to delight in doing the will of God, with his law written within your heart. That is the opposite of the ignorance Paul warned the Corinthians about when he wrote, “I would not have you ignorant.”

precepts.text: He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.
precepts.point: Brothers, a sister in pants should infuriate you, not catch your eye; the Lord of Israel is the belt doing the whipping now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
John says “the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Who is he that doeth the will of God? David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.

That one abides for ever: you will have everlasting life, and you are going to rule over these kingdoms. Everything you could not see yourself living without in this world shall come to an end, but the one with God's law in his heart abides.

So you must hate this world and everything in it. Brothers, you have to hate even the sight of a sister in pants, to the point where it infuriates you instead of catching your eye. The YNs, the young nuisances walking around in the community, should infuriate you. Bring back the belt. But we have a belt: the God of Israel, and he is doing the whipping right now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom in captivity.

Love not the world. Delight in his law, do his will, and abide for ever.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, yea thy law is within my heart: God's will is his laws.
precepts.point: The publican went home justified rather than the other. Everyone that exalts himself shall be abased, as Manasseh was locked up, and he that humbles himself shall be exalted, as Manasseh was later; and you will not like the humbling.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh confesses, “I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments.” Those two go together, because the Lord's will is his commandments. David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

To do God's will is to have his law in your heart. The laws of God are the will of God; God's will is his laws. So when Manasseh says he did not God's will, he is saying the same thing twice: he did not keep the commandments. Not doing the will of God is not some mystery feeling; it is breaking his law.

That is why Manasseh goes straight on to say, “I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.” He had provoked the Lord's wrath and done evil before him, and he was bowed down with iron bands, locked up with no release. A man who delights to do God's will keeps the law within his heart; Manasseh had to come to that by being humbled, bowing the knee of his heart and acknowledging his iniquity.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will; thy law is within my heart. God defines his will as his law, which is what the servant in Luke 12:47 knew and did not do.
precepts.point: To whom men have committed much, they will ask the more. If you have skills that can fill offices, more offices will be committed to you. If you cannot be used you are useless. Upper leadership keeps the phone on twenty-four hours a day because there is that much going on across Israel.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Christ says “that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.” What is the will of God? David defines it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

God defines his will as his law. His will for us is that we keep the commandments. So the servant in Luke 12:47 who knew his Lord's will is the one who knew the laws of God and prepared not himself.

Preparing yourself means measuring yourself against the Bible, men and women alike. The Bible is the measuring barometer we look at to see whether we are pairing ourselves off right with God. If we are really honest and examine ourselves, in many cases we are not: if Christ came back right now, many of us are not ready. It comes down to opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing what it says.

Much was given to us. We have the keys to the kingdom of heaven: the will of God, which people live a whole life and never understand, thinking a Hail Mary or gospel songs will have them holding hands with Jesus in the kingdom, not knowing that believing is an action word. Because we know his will, much more will be required of us, and as you move up in rank the road gets narrower until you have to walk blameless. We tell the people to do this and not do that, so we had better live it, or we will be beaten with many stripes.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: David learned the spirit that God does not care about sacrifice but obedience.
precepts.point: Whosoever shall keep the whole law and yet offend in one point is guilty of all: the Christian says you cannot keep them, but the context is the royal law, as the next verse shows, he that said do not commit adultery said also do not kill. Speak and do as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty, since Christ redeemed us from the death the moral law carried; he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.” This is quoted again in Hebrews 10.

David is saying, you opened my ears, and I understand the spirit: you don’t really care about sacrifices. Remember David wanted to build the temple. But the spirit was revealed to him that the sacrifices were just a placeholder for Christ to show up. He learned that because Christ was speaking through him.

So David realized: you don’t care about sacrifices at all, you care about obedience. That is what Samuel told Saul when he was king, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” And it is why the royal law of James 2, loving the neighbour and not being a respecter of persons, is what God is looking for.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. So what is the will of God? The laws of God. So what is it that pleased God in David, to the point that he established David as ruler over not only his sovereign country but his people as a sovereign government? He pleased the Lord in keeping God's commandments. He kept the commandments. He kept the testimonies.
precepts.point: Which shall fulfil all my will. Which shall fulfil all the Lord's will. Not your own personal will, not your own personal desire. The Lord establishes his rulers by who is faithful to him. Who is faithful to the commandments.

note.label: Sovereign Idiocracy

precepts.why:
Why is it that the Lord established David over his people, to establish the sovereign kingdom of Israel? If you want to be sovereign, there is one way to it: a one-way road with one victory at the end of it, the kingdom of heaven.

“And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis.” Even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish him. “And when he had removed him”: the Lord removed Saul from being king over Israel. So where does this power and authority come from? Only from God. Only God can make you sovereign and remove your sovereignty; not you, and not your piece of paper with weird words on it. “he raised up unto them David to be their king”: as righteous and powerful and mighty as David was, it was still the Lord that established him as king over Israel, a sovereign government.

“I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.” That is the caveat to being sovereign, to ruling over God's heritage: a man after God's own heart, exactly how the Lord wanted his servant and king to be. And he fulfils all the Lord's will, not his own personal will or desire.

What is the will of God? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. What pleased God in David, to the point that he established him as ruler over his people as a sovereign government? He kept God's commandments; he kept the testimonies. The Lord establishes his rulers by who is faithful to him, faithful to the commandments.

precepts.text: Forget not the law, but let thine heart keep the commandments, for length of days and long life and peace shall they add to thee.
precepts.point: The Lord brought him up out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set his feet upon a rock. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, and established his goings.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.” The Lord only hears the cry of those keeping the commandments, so even while afflicted David kept pushing and kept the commandments, rather than saying I already sinned, I might as well keep sinning. Solomon gives the counsel David followed: “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.”

Keep the commandments in the heart through the affliction, and length of days, long life and peace are added. That is the pardon David got: the Lord “brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.”

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not to thine own understanding; in all thy ways acknowledge him and he shall direct thy paths. David leaned on his own understanding, went off for a minute, then returned and applied this.
precepts.point: The Lord brought him up out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set his feet upon a rock. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, and established his goings.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.” David leaned on his own understanding, went off for a minute, then returned and applied this. He waited patiently, trusted the Lord with all his heart, and the Lord “inclined unto me, and heard my cry.”

Acknowledging him in all thy ways is what brought David up out of the horrible pit and the miry clay. The Lord lifted up his spirit, gave him the pardon, set his feet upon a rock and “established my goings”: he directed his paths, just as Solomon said.

precepts.text: The Lord delights in obeying his voice more than in burnt offerings and sacrifices; to obey is better than sacrifice and to hearken than the fat of rams.
precepts.point: Even in David's time he understood that sacrifice and offering were not what the Lord desired. There are multiple places where the Lord was not looking for the sacrifices.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.” Even in David's time he understood that sacrifice and offering were not what the Lord desired. Samuel said the same: “Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

There are multiple places where the Lord was not looking for the sacrifices. Sacrifice is really just a show of your obedience; obeying his voice is what he delights in. “mine ears hast thou opened”: the opened ear that hearkens is worth more than the fat of rams.

precepts.text: The law had a shadow of good things; those sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers perfect, and in them is a remembrance again made of sins every year. The Lord wants obedience over sacrifice.
precepts.point: Even in David's time he understood that sacrifice and offering were not what the Lord desired. There are multiple places where the Lord was not looking for the sacrifices.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” If they could, “would they not have ceased to be offered?” Instead, “in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.” The sacrifices offered year by year could never make the comers perfect; they only brought the sins back to mind each year. The Lord wants obedience over sacrifice, which is why David says “burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required.”

Sacrifice is just a show of your obedience. The Pharisees liked to say you could not get the kingdom without sacrifice, but they did not keep the commandments; they were all show and all talk, so they were the ones who could not make it to the kingdom.

precepts.text: "I will declare thy name unto my brethren; in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee." The congregation is the seed of Jacob, the seed of Israel, the Israelites, not any other nation. If you are thinking of Esau or Ishmael or any other nation, it is not referring to them.
precepts.point: David preached righteousness in the great congregation and did not refrain his lips. The great congregation is Israel, Zion, not any other nation or people.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“I have preached righteousness in the great congregation”. Who is the great congregation? “I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. Ye that fear the Lord, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.” The congregation is the seed of Jacob, the seed of Israel: the Israelites, not any other nation. If you are thinking of Esau or Ishmael or any other nation, it is not referring to them.

So the great congregation is Israel, Zion. David did not refrain his lips or hide the Lord's righteousness within his heart; he declared “thy faithfulness and thy salvation”, his lovingkindness and his truth, to his brethren, the Israelites.

precepts.text: His lovers and friends stood aloof from his sore, his kinsmen stood afar off, and those who sought his life laid snares and spoke mischievous things; but he was as a deaf and dumb man who opened not his mouth, having no room to speak for what he did.
precepts.point: David asks the Lord to make haste to help him and to put to shame those who seek after his soul to destroy it, and those who say "Aha" to mock him for his transgressions.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it”. Psalm 38 shows who they were: “My lovers and my friends stand aloof from my sore; and my kinsmen stand afar off. They also that seek after my life lay snares for me: and they that seek my hurt speak mischievous things, and imagine deceits all the day long.” His own lovers and friends stood aloof, his kinsmen stood afar off, and those who sought his life laid snares and spoke mischievous things.

And David could say nothing back. He was as a deaf and dumb man who opened not his mouth, because he had no room to speak for what he did. The ones who said to him “Aha, aha” were mocking him for his transgressions, so he does not answer them himself; he asks the Lord to “make haste to help me” and to drive them backward and put them to shame.

precepts.text: "Say unto my soul, I am thy salvation." Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek his soul; let them be as chaff before the wind and let the angel of the Lord chase them. This applies to our enemies to this day: look at the education systems and the conditions of our people; every nation outside the Israelites is trying to hide a net for our soul.
precepts.point: David asks the Lord to make haste to help him and to put to shame those who seek after his soul to destroy it, and those who say "Aha" to mock him for his transgressions.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
“Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me.” Psalm 35 is the same prayer: “Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation. Let them be confounded and put to shame that seek after my soul: let them be turned back and brought to confusion that devise my hurt. Let them be as chaff before the wind: and let the angel of the Lord chase them. Let their way be dark and slippery: and let the angel of the Lord persecute them.”

Every nation outside the Israelites falls in this category, seeking the heart of the Israelites without cause. It applies to our enemies to this day: look at the education systems and the conditions of our people; every nation outside the Israelites is trying to hide a net for our soul. So we say what David said: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation, and let the angel of the Lord chase them as chaff before the wind.

precepts.text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth, lest the Lord see it and turn his wrath away from him. That wrath then turns onto you, even if the enemy is one of your own people you have issues with.
precepts.point: Every nation outside the Israelites falls in this category, seeking the heart of the Israelites without cause.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

precepts.why:
David prays for his enemies to be “driven backward and put to shame”, but there is a line we cannot cross: “Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth: Lest the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.”

If you rejoice when the enemy falls, the Lord turns his wrath away from him, and that wrath then turns onto you. That holds even if the enemy is one of your own people you have issues with. Leave the shaming to the Lord, and do not be glad over it.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God; if you are doing God's will you will do the laws of God.
precepts.point: Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“As he loved cursing, so let it come unto him: as he delighted not in blessing, so let it be far from him.” Set against that is David: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

If you are doing God's will you will do the laws of God. The one who delights not in blessing but loves cursing is the nations doing their own will against the Israelites, afflicting the poor.

precepts.text: To do the will of the Most High is to keep His law, which is within the heart.
precepts.point: He prays, teach me to do thy will, for thou art my God; thy spirit is good. The will of the Most High is to keep His commandments, and His spirit is the word.

note.label: Psalm 143: Seeking the Old Paths in Affliction

precepts.why: “Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God”. “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” To do the will of the Most High is to keep his law, which is within the heart. The will of the Most High is to keep his commandments.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. That is the will of the Father, and the foolish did not have it.
precepts.point: Calling on his name while breaking the commandments is exactly this. Men bless what the law calls an abomination and still say Lord, Lord.

note.label: Matthew 25: The Ten Virgins, the Talents, and the Sheep and the Goats

precepts.why:
What is the will of the Father that the foolish did not do? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of the Father is his law, kept in the heart.

That is the oil the wise took in their vessels with their lamps, the wisdom of the scriptures, and the foolish did not have it. When the cry came at midnight, the wise were ready and went in with the bridegroom, and the foolish were left outside saying Lord, Lord. Watch therefore: have the law within your heart, because no one knows the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God, and thy law is within my heart, showing there is a spirit in a man that teaches the doctrine.
precepts.point: Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” Doing his will is the law within the heart, and there is a spirit in a man that teaches the doctrine.

You cannot push the spirit out. When you keep the Most High's laws and stay in the scriptures, the spirit animates your teaching with boldness. That is what the rulers saw in Peter and John: unlearned men with the law within them.

That is his will. So in 1 John 5:14, if we ask anything according to his will, he heareth us.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

points: David asks the Lord to make haste to help him and to put to shame those who seek after his soul to destroy it, and those who say "Aha" to mock him for his transgressions.

note.label: Psalm 40: Patient Waiting, Obedience Over Sacrifice, and the Great Congregation

points: Let those who seek the Lord rejoice and be glad, and let those who love his salvation say continually, the Lord be magnified. Though David is poor and needy, the Lord thinks upon him; the Lord is his help and his deliverer.
